snapshot.capital_scaled: ₹2–10 crore for a team, prototypes, certification and early production
snapshot.margin_production: Services and pilots often fund the early years
snapshot.distribution_note: Sales are to governments, large companies and defence, with long buying cycles

tailwinds: Drones, robotics, space and defence are priority sectors with government support and liberalised rules.
Grants from DST, iDEX (defence), BIRAC and state programmes fund early research.
IIT and university incubators offer labs and mentors.
Large companies and governments are looking for Indian suppliers instead of imports.
headwinds: Hardware takes years and a lot of money to develop.
Buyers such as governments and defence take a long time to decide.
Certification and testing can take months.
Talent in robotics, electronics and AI is expensive and scarce.
angle_2026: India's drone rules, defence procurement from startups through iDEX, and the space sector reforms have opened markets that were closed a few years ago. In 2026, the deeptech startups that succeed pick one buyer with a painful, expensive problem and use grants and paid pilots to fund development.
cost_basis: Estimated for a team of 3–6 engineers building to a working prototype and first pilots, 2026 prices.

setup_costs.covers: Type certification, safety tests, field trials

unit_economics.example: For a ₹5 lakh industrial robot or drone system:
rows: ₹1,00,000–2,00,000 per unit before R&D and sales
unit_economics.note: Software, maintenance contracts and data services often make the business work. Plan for recurring revenue alongside hardware sales.

investor_probes: Who is the buyer, and have they paid for a pilot?
How long until you have a certified product?
What does each unit cost to make at 100 units?
What stops a large company copying you?
bootstrap_takeaway: Win grants and a paid pilot before raising equity. A paying customer and a working prototype make the first funding round much easier.
licences: Company registration and DPIIT startup recognition
Drone registration and type certification under the Drone Rules, 2021, for drones

hard_truths.title: It takes years
hard_truths.text: Most hardware startups take 3–5 years to reach steady revenue. Plan your funding for that.

hard_truths.title: Pilots don't always convert
hard_truths.text: Many pilots end without a purchase order. Ask for paid pilots with clear success criteria.

hard_truths.title: Talent is scarce
hard_truths.text: Good engineers are in demand. Equity, mission and interesting problems help you compete.

hard_truths.title: Scaling production is hard
hard_truths.text: Making ten units is very different from making a thousand. Plan manufacturing early.

plan_goal: The aim is a working prototype, one grant application and a signed pilot with a paying buyer.

plan.title: Validate the problem
steps: Talk to 20 potential buyers about the problem and what it costs them.
Map which grants and programmes fit.

plan.title: Prototype
steps: File a provisional patent if there's something new.

plan.title: Review
steps: Decide on grants, angel funding or more pilots.
